passages.context: Psalm 88, Sermo II, section 12, complete. The printed section explicitly heads its lemma vers. 51, Memento, Domine, opprobrii, servorum tuorum. The passage interprets the reproaches borne by Christians in the light of Christ and the Church.
passages.notes: Copied mechanically, without retyping or normalization, from the whole LF-delimited line 190 of the hash-checked retained part-9 Latin artifact. Read section 12 in the context of the Sermo II heading and sections 11-14. Compared the complete paragraph directly with PL 37, col. 1139, PDF page 63 of artifact.jacques-paul-migne.patrologia-latina-volume-37.paris-1845.internet-archive-google-pdf-afe6878f after retrieving the complete PDF and matching its registered SHA-256 afe6878f6241d34824942b0f057537b208f67978d36c94cbf251d9b0de397bb4. The lexical text agrees; the web transcription has its own quotation punctuation, expands print line-break hyphenation, and omits the apparatus marker after loquitur and the footnote beneath the column. This is the identified web transcription checked against the historical printing, not a diplomatic facsimile transcription or a modern critical text. The existing page-only passage passage.augustine.enarrationes-in-psalmos.latin-migne-pl37-paris-1845.88-sermo-ii-12 identifies the same locus under the print edition and must not be admitted as a second independent commentary witness. Composition-date evidence: the complete Augustinian Tavola cronologica at https://www.augustinus.it/italiano/esposizioni_salmi/tavola_cronologica.htm, retrieved and read 2026-10-23, row 88, s. 1-2, reports Zarb 411-412 at Hippo and Rondet 411 at Carthage. Its notes identify S. Zarb, Chronologia Enarrationum S. Augustini in Psalmos (Malta, 1948), pp. 253-256, and H. Rondet, Notes de exegese augustinienne, Recherches de Science religieuse 39 (1951), pp. 472-477. Those studies were not themselves consulted. A bounded 411-412 dating is therefore a sourced chronology-table proposal; the place remains disputed. It dates this discourse, not the entire Enarrationes collection or the Migne printing.
